This binding is followed by Adra1b participating in the activity of the alpha-adrenergic receptor, which in turn is participated by Adra2c. This chain of interactions implies that Loxapine may influence the function of Adra2c through its effect on Adra1b, potentially modulating the activity of the alpha-adrenergic receptor complex. The integration of these pathways suggests a possible functional link between Loxapine and Adra2c, though the exact mechanism of this interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
